timecoded_text_to_speech.text: Hello and welcome to Wild Country Adventures Campground Review.
Today we're in Douglas County at Amna-Con Falls State Park Campground situated along the
Amna-Con River.
Amna-Con Falls Campground is open year round and features 36 reservable campsites, although
I was only able to find 35 with site 35 being an ABA site for people with disabilities.
Sites 32 and 33 are group sites and sites 16 and 17 are hiking sites.
Each campsite will cost you $15 per night, however all campsites are reservable so you'll
need to tack on another $10.75 for a reservation fee.
Unless of course you're lucky enough to just stop by and they happen to have a site available.
But remember, there are no power hookups or showers at Amna-Con Falls so plan your trip
accordingly.
Each campsite will come equipped with a fire pit and a picnic table.
You'll also find pit toilets by sites 8, 15 and 35.
Drinking water is also available by all three pit toilets.
You'll also find a swing set and sandbox a little ways off from site 13.
You'll also find plenty of amazing sites here at Amna-Con Falls State Park which happens
to be located along the Douglas Falls.
Amna-Con Falls has a total of four waterfalls with upper falls, lower falls, snake pit falls,
and of course now and then falls.
You'll also find the Horton-Covered Footbridge which spans 55 feet as it crosses the Amna-Con
River just above lower falls.
In fact, this is one of six bow-strong bridges that still exists today.
You'll even find a selfie station that overlooks the lower falls.
Not to mention an abundance of picnic tables with grills scattered throughout the park.
And you'll also find plenty of adventure in Douglas County with great fishing for musky,
walleye, pipe, bass, and pan fish.
Not to mention Douglas County offers exceptional hunting opportunities for bare, deer, fisher,
sharp tailed grouse, turkey, and of course, small game.
You'll also find beautiful hiking, biking, and ATV trails, amazing fall colors, stunning
landscape, and long winding country roads.
And if that wasn't enough, you're also 25 minutes from Paterson State Park which of course
has little Manitou Falls and Big Manitou Falls which is the largest waterfall in Wisconsin
at 165 feet.
So whatever your adventure you bound to find in an abundance here in Douglas County,
so why not make Amna-Con Falls State Park your base camp.
But remember, be respectful, pack out your trash, and leave the area ready for the next
adventure seeker.
Hopefully we'll see you out there.

youtube_description:
Hello and welcome to Wild Country Adventures Campground Review. In this video we'll be in Douglas County at Amnicon Falls State Park Campground. Amnicon Falls has a total of 35 sites with one ADA site, a group site, and two walk in sites. You'll also find 4 waterfalls within the park with, Upper Falls, Lower Falls, Snake Pit Falls, and Now and Then Falls, but depending on water levels Now and Then Falls may be dry. The campground itself can accommodate a 30 foot rig but you won't find power hook ups, dump, or fill stations here. Firewood is for sale at the camp office but only during business hours.

And Don't Click This Link: https://www.youtube.com/c/WildCountryAdventures?sub_confirmation=1
